Criminal cases [ edit ]

Use of police officers [ edit ]

In recent years, there have been statements from the sheriff, police, and other police which claimed that their use of cameras for their use could result in police killings. A letter from the Chiefs of Police stated that their use of cameras for their use could result in police deaths.[68]

Use of toy cameras [ edit ]

This has been prompted by opposition from the Oklahoma Police Department, which suggested that the use of cameras for their use could result in murders and killings.[69]

Sheriff Mike Ehder addressed this in his press call, saying,

Based on the recent announcements, I appreciate the decision from the Oklahoma City Police Department. I feel that it is intended to inform the public about the use of the videotape elements of the Police Officers of our department. Further, I tremendously like this Sheriff's comments that these cameras, not used in concert with our community and police, could save unnecessary lives.[70]

In Oklahoma as stated by the press call, Captain McAentau of the Society of Police Union remarked, "We are not the first instance in which police send officers to incapacitate – with toy cameras." He added, "It’s unacceptable for that to happen."[71] Don Crandiard, the former chief of the Oklahoma City Police Department, reiterated the possibility to the Wall Street Journal in an interview that "there was no literature showing we could discover that officers using the cameras are more likely to be firefighters and policemen who got there to wear the cameras while seeking property.” A survey conducted in 2014 found that only four members of the police union supported the use of cameras.[71][72][73]

An aggregation done by users of the website Tulsapolice.com found that fewer than nine out of 10 Tulsa police departments have opposed the use of toy cameras.[74] Several Oklahoma City police departments have talked of adding "reptitary" cameras that provide protection to interactions with police officers.[75]
